case_name: Sir Mortimer B. Davis Jewish General Hospital (CIUSSS du Centre-Ouest-de-l'Île-de-Montréal) c. W.T.
text:
Sir Mortimer B. Davis Jewish
General Hospital (CIUSSS du Centre-Ouest-de-l'Île-de-Montréal) c. W.T.

2021 QCCS 2757

SUPERIOR COURT

CANADA

PROVINCE
OF QUEBEC

DISTRICT OF

MONTREAL

N° :

500-17-117188-212

DATE :

June 29, 2021

BEFORE THE HONOURABLE GEETA
NARANG, J.C.S.

SIR MORTIMER B.
DAVIS JEWISH GENERAL HOSPITAL,
administered
by the
CIUSSS DU CENTRE-OUEST-DE-L’ÎLE-DE-MONTRÉAL

and

DR. LOUISE MINER

Plaintiffs

vs

W. T.

Defendant

and

C. C.

Interested
Person

and

R. T.

Interested Person

____________________________________________________________________

ORDER FOR THE AUTHORIZATION OF CARE

____________________________________________________________________

[
1
]

Mr. T. appeared before the Court by Teams.

[
2
]

The Sir Mortimer B. Jewish General Hospital (the “Hospital”) is asking
the Court to make decisions regarding where Mr. T. will live for the next two
years.

[
3
]

Mr. T. is a proud man who explained to the Court that he wants to go
home. He used the word “jail” several times when the Hospital’s recommendations
were discussed.

[
4
]

An English-Cantonese interpreter assisted throughout the hearing, though
Mr. T. managed to communicate in English on several occasions.

[
5
]

Mr. T. has been at the Hospital since March 18
th
2021. It
appears that a family member brought him there.

[
6
]

The Court of Quebec has rendered five judgments concerning Mr. T.
ordering both psychiatric assessment and his confinement. The last judgment was
rendered on June 1
st
, 2021 and it lapses on July 1
st
, 2021.
[1]

[
7
]

Mr. T. has been charged with uttering death threats pursuant to
section
264.1 (1)
(a) and
(2)
(b) of the
Criminal Code
[2]
following an altercation with his wife.
[3]

[
8
]

Family members were served with the Hospital’s Application for
Authorization for Care, but were not present at the hearing.

[
9
]

As is often the case in applications of this nature, the Court relied
heavily on expert testimony and expert reports in deciding this matter.

[
10
]

Dr. Sandra Popescu-Crainic was qualified as an expert
in geriatric medicine and Ms. Jacqueline Bolofer was qualified as an expert in
social work. They provided their opinions regarding Mr. T.’s capacity to
consent to care and the living arrangements that are being proposed by the
Hospital.

[
11
]

Unfortunately, neither experts’
curriculum vitae
was appended to
their reports.
[4]

[
12
]

The Court asked both Dr. Popescu-Crainic and Ms.
Bolofer to read the
Declaration Regarding the Carrying out of the Mission of
an Expert
established by the Minister of Justice pursuant to article 235 of
the
Code of Civil Procedure
.

[
13
]

Then, after hearing of their education and experience,
the Court was satisfied that they are able to provide objective expert evidence
regarding the matter at hand.

[
14
]

In deciding whether to grant the Hospital’s Application and authorize
the proposed placement plan, the Court will address the following two
questions:
[5]

1)

Should the Court be making decisions regarding Mr. T.’s care?

2)

Is the proposed placement plan in Mr. T.’s best interests?

(1)

Should the Court be making decisions regarding Mr. T.’s care?

[
15
]

In Dr. Popescu-Crainic’s opinion, Mr. T. suffers from a major
cognitive disorder which, in the past, would have been called “dementia”,
though the term is no longer used in the current Diagnostic and Statistical
Manuel of Mental Disorders.

[
16
]

His illness is aggravated by the consumption of
alcohol. When he drinks, the behavioural manifestations of his illness include
serious aggressivity.

[
17
]

When Mr. T. was first admitted to the Hospital, medical
personnel attempted to identify reversible causes of Mr. T.’s cognitive
disorder. Blood work and a brain scan were done. Unfortunately, no reversible
causes were identified. Mr. T.’s cognitive deficits have not improved since his
admission.

[
18
]

Based on Dr. Popescu-Crainic’s opinion, Ms. Bolofer’s
observations and exchanges with Mr. T. at the hearing, the Court finds that he
is incapable of consenting to his care.

[
19
]

He does not have the capacity to understand why
returning to his duplex might be problematic, even though, when he drinks, he
is aggressive with his wife and he cannot be in contact with her because of the
pending criminal charges.

[
20
]

When the issue of where he should live is discussed, Mr. T. simply repeats that he owns a duplex and enunciates the primal
desire to “go home”.

[
21
]

He is unaware of the risks that come with returning to
his residence, including being in breach of his conditions.

[
22
]

His inability to comprehend the issues that will result
from moving back to his duplex are caused by the major cognitive disorder from
which he suffers.

[
23
]

Dr. Popescu-Crainic and Ms. Bolofer both testified
that, every now and then, Mr. T. appears to be open to being placed and living
in an “intermediate resource” (commonly called a “
ressource
intermédiaire
” or “RI”), but refuses to sign the required documents and
changes his mind afterwards.

[
24
]

Based on the experts’ evidence and exchanges with Mr. T.
at the hearing, both in English and through the interpreter, the Court is of
the opinion that he is refusing the proposed placement plan.

[
25
]

His sons and his wife decided not to attend the hearing.

[
26
]

Given Mr. T.’s incapacity and his family’s absence at the hearing, the
Court will step in and decide whether the Hospital’s plan is in Mr. T.’s best
interests.
[6]

(2)

Is the proposed placement plan in Mr. T.’s best
interests?

[
27
]

In Ms. Bolofer’s expert opinion, there are numerous risk factors
associated with allowing Mr. T. to return to the community, including:

➢

His cognitive decline;

➢

Serious issues with his short-term memory;

➢

Complications due to the pending criminal proceedings;

➢

His family’s inability to provide the assistance he needs;

➢

His inability to perform tasks needed for daily living such as
feeding himself, bathing and dressing;

➢

His access to alcohol in the community and the aggressivity that results
for alcohol consumption.

[
28
]

Given these factors, the Court is convinced that living in a facility
where he can be supported by professionals is in his best interests.

[
29
]

The drawback of such an arrangement is that it is not what Mr. T. wants.
However, at this point, his wishes simply cannot be respected without putting
him in harm’s way.

[
30
]

The Hospital is asking for an order of two years and the Court finds
this term to be reasonable in the circumstances, particularly given Mr. T.’s
continued cognitive decline.

[
31
]

Finally, the Court is of the opinion the orders rendered should be executory
notwithstanding appeal.

[
32
]

The last confinement of the Court of Quebec lapses on July 1
st

2021 and, if Mr. T. is released from the Hospital in the coming days, there is
nowhere for him to go: his family does not have the resources to provide for
his care; he does not have the skills to care for himself; and, because of the
pending matter at Municipal Court, he cannot return to his home.

[
33
]

FOR THESE REASONS, THE COURT:

[
34
]

GRANTS
the
present Application;

[
35
]

AUTHORIZES

Plaintiffs to provide the necessary documents and information contained in
Defendant
’
s medical record to the Court for the purpose of the Application;

[
36
]

EXEMPTS
Plaintiffs from serving the
present Application to Defendant;

[
37
]

AUTHORIZES
Plaintiffs to notify the
present Application to Defendant by delivery in person;

[
38
]

CONFIRMS
Defendant
’
s incapacity to consent to the placement plan;

[
39
]

AUTHORIZES
Plaintiffs
to place Defendant in the least restrictive supervised resource approved by his
treating team, where his safety, necessary care and daily needs can be met.
This could include an intermediate resource (“ressource intermédiaire (RI)”),
as appropriate given Defendant’s condition, where Defendant’s highest possible
level of autonomy can be safeguarded;

[
40
]

AUTHORIZES
the
administrator of the designated supervised facility to lodge Defendant despite
his refusal, by using all appropriate measures, for the duration of the
judgment;

[
41
]

AUTHORIZES
Plaintiffs
to pursue Defendant’s hospitalization until a safe discharge plan is in place and
in accordance with the placement plan described above;

[
42
]

ORDERS
that if
Defendant’s condition deteriorates or if he fails to comply with the placement
plan or if he can no longer live in the designated resource approved by his
treating team, he be transported to the Sir Mortimer B. Davis Jewish General
Hospital or to any other hospital setting by ambulance or a peace officer, upon
request of any member of his treating team and be hospitalized so that medical
conditions may be assessed and stabilized, until his condition allows his
discharge, which shall be for the shortest period possible according to his
condition;

[
43
]

ORDERS
any peace
officer to use the necessary means, including the necessary force, to assist
Plaintiffs or any institution or physician or person designated by them in the
execution of the judgment if Defendant refuses to comply with the judgment;

[
44
]

ORDERS
any
treating physician of Defendant to report, every twelve (12) months, to the
Counsel of Physicians, Dentists and Pharmacists ("CPDP") of the
CIUSSS du Centre-Ouest-de-l’Île-de-Montréal or to the CPDP of any other
institution designated by the Plaintiffs on the evolution of Defendant's health
and his general condition;

[
45
]

ORDERS
that, in
case of diverging opinions between Defendant
’
s treating
physician and the CPDP, the difference of opinion be submitted to this Honourable
Court;

[
46
]

ORDERS
that the
conclusions of the judgment be applicable with the necessary adjustments by any
health institution, treating team and/or treating doctor in charge of
Defendant;

[
47
]

ORDERS
that the
judgment be valid for a duration of
two (2) years
;

[
48
]

THE WHOLE
,
without legal costs.

__________________________________

GEETA NARANG, J.C.S.

M
tre

Andréane Baribeau

Attorney for the
Plaintiff

Mr. W. T.

[1]
The Court of Quebec file number is [...]. The judgments were
produced as Exhibit P-3,
en liasse
.

[2]

RSC 1985, c C-46
.

[3]
At the hearing, many references were made to this matter, but
no documentary evidence regarding the case was filed. As such, the Court asked
that M
tre
Baribeau, counsel for the Hospital, provide the Court with
such documentary evidence and she did so. The
Dénonciation
in Municipal Court
number [...], as well as the
plumitif
, was sent to the Court.

[4]
Exhibits P-1 and P-2.

[5]

F.D. c. Centre universitaire de santé McGill
,
2015 QCCA
1139
and article 16 of the
Québec Civil Code.

[6]
Article 16 of the
Québec Civil Code
provides that: "T
he
authorization of the court is necessary where the person who may give consent
to care required by the state of health of a minor or a person of full age who
is incapable of giving his consent is prevented from doing so or, without
justification, refuses to do so; it is also necessary where a person of full
age who is incapable of giving his consent categorically refuses to receive
care, except in the case of hygienic care or emergency.”
